basics.name: Xiaoyan Guo (Flora)
basics.label: Student
basics.summary: Research interests include AI-assisted software engineering, large language models, software testing, and program analysis. Incoming PhD student at the University of Virginia.

work.name: University of Science and Technology of China
work.summary: Explored research topics in artificial intelligence and large language models, later focusing on software engineering and LLM-assisted software development.

work.name: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
work.summary: Research on AI-driven multi-agent systems for adaptive code completion and AI-assisted software development.

education.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

publications.name: Enhancing Multi-Modal LLMs Reasoning via Difficulty-Aware Group Normalization
publications.summary: Proposed a difficulty-aware group normalization method to improve multimodal LLM reasoning in reinforcement learning settings.

publications.name: Multi-Agent Systems for Dataset Adaptation in Software Engineering Capabilities, Limitations, and Future Directions
publications.summary: Studied the effectiveness and limitations of multi-agent systems for adapting code completion methods to unseen software engineering datasets.

projects.name: AI-Driven Multi-Agent Frameworks for Adaptive Code Completion
projects.summary: Research on adaptive multi-agent systems for AI-assisted code completion and automated prompt engineering.
highlights: Evaluated cross-project adaptation and robustness of multi-agent code completion systems.
Developed prompt-fixing strategies and automated evaluation workflows.
Built a VSCode extension for Python-based GitHub Copilot interaction.

projects.name: Enhancing MLLMs Reasoning via Difficulty-Aware Group Normalization
projects.summary: Research on improving multimodal large language model reasoning with difficulty-aware reinforcement learning strategies.
highlights: Designed difficulty-aware regrouping methods for RLVR training.
Evaluated performance across multimodal reasoning benchmarks.
Achieved consistent improvements over GRPO/DAPO baselines.

projects.name: Knowledge-Enhanced Agents Based on RAG and Web Search in LLM
projects.summary: Developed knowledge-grounded LLM agents integrating retrieval-augmented generation and real-time web search.
highlights: Led implementation of the WebSearch subsystem with dual-agent architecture.
Developed plugins for Google Search, Google Scholar, and arXiv integration.
Enhanced retrieval and planning modules for grounded generation.
